lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 17 years old. He lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 17-year-old son named Alex who lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17, a key factor in determining eligibility is whether he's in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in full-time education at school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that to be honest. I don't know if what he's doing counts as approved education or training or not. He does go to college, but I'm not certain if that's the right type.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. It's helpful to know that Alex is attending college.

To help determine if his college course would count as approved education or training for Child Benefit purposes, could you tell me: **Is Alex attending college full-time or part-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know whether it's full-time or part-time. I'm not really clear on the details of his course arrangement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it can sometimes be difficult to know all the details of your child's educational arrangements.

Let me ask a few more questions to see if we can establish eligibility another way:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Now, let me ask: **Are you responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and/or provide financial support for him such as food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives at home with me, so I'm definitely responsible for him. I provide for all his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Let me also check: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or started claiming benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He doesn't work 24 hours a week or more, and he's not claiming any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment: **Do you or your partner (if you have one) have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another status that gives you the right to live here?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to reside in the UK.

Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's the situation:**

You meet all the basic requirements:
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- You're responsible for Alex, who lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He's not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right

**However,** since Alex is 17 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in **approved education or training**. You've mentioned that Alex attends college, but you're not sure whether his course is full-time or part-time, or whether it qualifies as "approved education or training" under Child Benefit rules.

**What you can do next:**

1. **Find out more about Alex's college course** - Check with his college whether his course is considered full-time and whether it's an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes.

2. **Contact the Child Benefit Office** - They can help you determine whether Alex's specific college course qualifies. You can reach them through the contact details on the gov.uk website.

3. **Make a claim anyway** - You could submit a Child Benefit claim, and HMRC will assess whether Alex's education qualifies during the application process.

I hope this helps clarify your situation!
